Hi everyone,
I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.
If you would like to talk 1:1 this week, reply here and I will make time.
Thank you,
Leonard", "channel": "C0ADGSZKR3R", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}]}

Attached please find the materials for our upcoming board meeting, scheduled for Jan 14, Wednesday at 9:00 AM PT via Google Meet.

*Game Progress*
• _Combo Fighter_ is our best-performing prototype to date. Players are engaging deeply: ~55 min D0 playtime, ~53 mins average daily playtime, ~4 CPI on broad meta campaigns
• D1 retention is soft at 30% but we have clear levers: smoothing early difficulty, improving tutorial flow. We will also be adding basic monetization, and reducing CPI through creative changes (e.g. female character).
• We believe this is a promising foundation with potential to evolve into a scalable puzzle-RPG hybrid. However, it’s still too early to talk about the scalability of the title. 
*Company Building*
We have $25K cash in the bank and our runway ends at the end of this month. If There is appetite for [PERSON_NAME_2000] to re-evaluate under the light of the promising metrics, we’re asking [PERSON_NAME_2000] to invest $500K. This gets us:
• 6 months of salary runway for the founding team and 4 employees.
• $170K in performance marketing to test ROAS viability.
If There’s no appetite to extend funding, we’d like to discuss winding down Harmony Games and transferring the IP into a new entity. This wouldn’t be material for [PERSON_NAME_2000], but it may give us a shot to make the game work on a leaner path that still creates value for our families.
Let us know your thoughts.
Best,
Leonard", "channel": "C07C2866011", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}]}

I’m reaching out because we are shutting down Harmony Games, Inc. and want
to make sure we execute an orderly wind-down properly.

We are a Delaware corporation, qualified to do business in North Carolina
and California. We have preferred stock from a seed round (no SAFEs). We
have no US employees other than ourselves and only 4 international
contractors. We are out of funds and want to avoid missteps around creditor
ha[USERNAME_11664], state Withdrawals, tax filings, and closing operational accounts
cleanly.

   -

   A practical wind-down plan and timeline
   -

   Vendor termination support
   -

   Creditor communications and claim handling approach
   -

   Delaware dissolution and withdrawals in CA and NC, plus tax/accounting
   closeout coordination
   -

   Guidance on reserves and any final distributions consistent with
   preferred stock terms

If this is in your wheelhouse, can we set up a short call this week? I can
share our current cash position, liabilities list, and key contracts in
advance.

Thank you,
Leonard Hayes"}}}, {"id": "robert@harmonygames.co/<CH2PR15MB3558F3E72D36311458EEB4BCDE62A@CH2PR15MB3558.namprd15.prod.outlook.com>", "threadId": "robert@harmonygames.co/1856689465442954434", "labelIds": ["SPAM", "CATEGORY_PERSONAL", "UNREAD"], "snippet": "Hello Leonard, Pleasure to meet you here via email. input.title: Combo Fighter — Honest Post-Mortem & Harmony Games Wind-Down Ledger (for the angel calls)
input.bodyText:
COMBO FIGHTER — HONEST POST-MORTEM & HARMONY GAMES WIND-DOWN LEDGER
Prepared by Robert (Co-Founder / Creative Director) — 28 Feb 2026
For: Leonard (angel calls) and Arthur. Source of truth for what the data actually said, what is still costing us, and where the money leaves us. Written from primary sources (Snowflake warehouse, wind-down Slack, finance tables) — not screenshots.

==============================================================
1. WHAT THE DATA ACTUALLY SAID ABOUT COMBO FIGHTER
==============================================================
Combo Fighter was my design — difficulty curve, card economy, all of it. So here is the unsmoothed version, better and worse than memory.

Window with real players: 5 Jan 2026 → 9 Feb 2026 (36 days). That is the full life; analytics events stop on 9 Feb.

ENGAGEMENT — genuinely strong (reads BETTER than the board framing):
- DAU grew from 45 on day one (5 Jan) to a peak of ~784 combined (Android+iOS) on 8–9 Feb — roughly 17x in five weeks.
- 55,101 total sessions over the life; ~3.5 sessions per DAU per day at ~12.7 min/session ≈ ~45 min of play per active user per day. That is consistent with the "~53 min daily playtime" we told the board.
- Day-1 retention averaged ~44% (range 37–51%). That is BETTER than the "soft 30%" reported to the board in January. D7 ~22%, D30 ~11% — decays but not catastrophic for an untuned prototype.
People who found the game liked it and played it a lot. The core loop worked.

MONETIZATION — the hard truth (reads WORSE):
- Lifetime revenue: $0.00. Not "low" — zero. IAP never shipped, ads never shipped. We were "adding basic monetization" the entire time and never did.
- Because there was $0 ARPU, there was no ROAS and no LTV signal. We literally never tested whether the game could make money.

ACQUISITION COST — ran higher than we said:
- Lifetime paid UA on Combo Fighter: $7,476 across six networks (Meta FB/IG, Unity Ads, Google UAC, ironSource, AppLovin), 1,341 attributed installs → blended CPI ≈ $5.58.
- The board deck cited "~$4 CPI on broad meta campaigns." Actuals ran ~40% higher than that, and against $0 revenue every dollar was pure cost.

HONEST VERDICT: Combo Fighter did not "fail on the data." It engaged well and its D1 was actually better than we reported. What killed it is that we ran out of runway before monetization ever went live, so we spent ~$7.5K acquiring users we never once tried to monetize, at a CPI north of $5.5. The game was never given the test that would have proven it out or killed it. That is the honest sentence for the wind-down letter.

==============================================================
2. WHAT IS STILL QUIETLY COSTING US (named, with figures + owners)
==============================================================
We voted to stop on 9 Feb. The subscription checklist got worked hard — but it only covered SaaS. Nobody went back over the money going OUT the door on the media side.

2a. THE LEAK NOBODY NAMED — LIVE PAID UA (highest priority)
The ad-spend ledger shows paid campaigns on ALL THREE apps still charging every single day from 10 Feb through 28 Feb (today). This is NOT on the cancellation checklist.
- Total spent AFTER the 9 Feb stop: $8,447 (1,541 installs), ~$445/day and still running.
   • Domino Delights: $5,574   • Combo Fighter: $2,441   • Zombie Match 3D: $432
- Networks still live: Meta FB/IG, Unity Ads, Google UAC, ironSource, AppLovin.
ACTION: verify against the live ad dashboards (Meta/Google/Unity/ironSource/AppLovin) and pause everything to $0 today. OWNER: Arthur (already handling MMP/Unity/data), with Leonard (set up the Meta app). This single item is larger than the entire SaaS cleanup and, if left running, breaks the "the P&L covers everything" conclusion.

2b. SAAS DELIBERATELY KEPT RUNNING (known, but still money)
- Metabase + dbt: ~$300/mo total — kept explicitly "until Robert stops caring about Combo Fighter data." This is running for MY benefit; I will call the cutoff so it doesn't drift. OWNER: Arthur/Robert.
- GitHub + Metabase moved onto Arthur's personal KubLLC card — now a PERSONAL cost to Arthur until data is extracted/transferred.
- Gusto, Deel, Intuit/QuickBooks (keep ~2 months), Slack (3 seats), Google (archive unused accts 15 Feb), Linear (transition), Figma (paid through 11 Sep, won't renew).
- Carta: renewal 15 Aug, tied to a Chase account we have CLOSED — this can bounce and turn into a collections/obligation item. Flag for the wind-down provider. OWNER: Leonard.
- Cancelled already: Helpshift, Layer, Soundly, Zapier, Cursor, CodeRabbit, Kapwing.

==============================================================
3. THE MONEY — DOES THE DATA DEAL COVER AN ORDERLY SHUTDOWN?
==============================================================
Cash on hand (28 Feb): $2,500. (Was $25K end-Jan.) The company is insolvent.

Incoming: data-LICENSING deal (structured as a license, not a sale, so we retain all IP) with the buyer.
- Gross cash: $22,500
- Fees/charge: $11,700
- NET to the estate: ≈ $10,800

Use of proceeds (per the wind-down channel): pay the SVB card in full and close it; Unity and Singular are being terminated at $0 on insolvency grounds (we used well under 1% of the Singular cap); small contractor gestures (~$600 Leapblock; Martin was paid out by the acquirer) are being covered by us personally.

WHERE THAT ACTUALLY LEAVES US — be precise:
- The number to carry is NOT $22.5K. After the $11,700 fee, only ~$10,800 actually reaches the shutdown, on top of ~$2,500 cash ≈ ~$13.3K of total dry powder.
- Management's read is that this "covers everything" and lets us file dissolution without a capital call. On paper that is true — but ONLY if (a) the SVB card payoff lands inside that ~$13K envelope, and (b) no new post-9-Feb costs appear.
- (b) is already false in spirit: the live UA in §2a ($8.4K and climbing) is real cash that is NOT in that P&L. If it isn't stopped, it eats most of the net data proceeds and the "covers everything" statement no longer holds.
- The SVB card balance itself is the swing variable and only appears in the P&L screenshots — it should be confirmed as a hard number before we treat this as break-even.

BOTTOM LINE: This is a break-even exit, not a distribution. Nothing comes back to the angels. The data deal roughly funds an orderly close IF — and only if — we kill the live UA now and the SVB payoff is inside ~$13K.

==============================================================
4. PERSONAL EXPOSURE (Leonard, Arthur, Robert)
==============================================================
We are officers/directors winding down a knowingly-insolvent Delaware C-corp. Obligations incurred or left running AFTER the 9 Feb shutdown decision are exactly the category that can attach to us personally. Two concrete ones already exist: the live UA still charging the (closing) card, and the Carta auto-renew tied to a closed account. Stop the UA, get the SVB number, and let Sherwood (the wind-down advisor) paper the Carta/Unity/Singular terminations. Find it now, not later.

==============================================================
5. THE 2–3 FIGURES TO LEAD WITH ON THE ANGEL CALLS
==============================================================
1. "$0 lifetime revenue on Combo Fighter — we ran out of runway before monetization ever shipped, so the business model was never actually tested." (The honest core.)
2. "Engagement was real: ~780 DAU and ~45 min/day in five weeks, D1 ~44%. The product worked; ~$5.58 CPI against $0 ARPU is what we couldn't outrun." (Credibility + the real constraint.)
3. "The wind-down is break-even, not a return: a $22.5K data license nets ~$10.8K after fees, which retires our bank card and closes us cleanly. No capital is coming back." (Sets expectations honestly.)

— Sources: ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS, ANALYTICS.MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY, ANALYTICS.MONETIZATION.REVENUE_DAILY, FINANCE.EXPENSES.CASH_BALANCE / MONTHLY_BURN, and the #wind-down Slack channel (data-deal terms, subscription canvas).

<@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> — I went back to the real numbers (Snowflake + our finance tables, not the pasted screenshots) and wrote up one honest account for the angel calls. Full doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/af3440008828e885c8bb52ed/edit

The three things that matter:

1) *Combo Fighter, unsmoothed.* Life was 5 Jan–9 Feb. Engagement was genuinely good — peaked ~780 DAU from 45 in five weeks, ~45 min/day, D1 actually ~44% (better than the 30% we told the board). But lifetime revenue was *$0.00* — monetization never shipped — and blended CPI ran *~$5.58* (we told the board ~$4). So it didn't fail on the data; we ran out of runway before we ever tested whether it could make money. That's the honest line for the letter.

2) *We are still bleeding cash that the cancellation list missed.* Paid UA on all three apps has been charging every day from 10 Feb through today — *$8,447 since the 9th* (~$445/day, still live): Domino $5,574, Combo Fighter $2,441, ZM3D $432. This is bigger than the entire SaaS cleanup and it's not on the checklist. <@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> can you pull up Meta/Google/Unity/ironSource/AppLovin and pause everything to $0 today? Filing a Linear item so it doesn't get lost between us.

3) *The money is break-even, not a cushion.* The $22.5K data license nets *~$10.8K* after the $11.7K fee; with $2.5K cash that's ~$13.3K of dry powder, all earmarked for the SVB card. It "covers everything" *only if* we kill the live UA above and the SVB payoff lands inside ~$13K. The number to carry is $10.8K net, not $22.5K. Nothing comes back to the angels.

Two loose ends flagged in the doc: Carta auto-renew 15 Aug is tied to the *closed* Chase account (bounce/collections risk), and GitHub+Metabase are now on Blake's personal KubLLC card.

input.description:
Owner check: Leonard, Arthur, Robert are personally on the hook for post-9-Feb obligations. This tracks everything still taking money from us that the subscription checklist missed. Full write-up: https://docs.google.com/document/d/af3440008828e885c8bb52ed/edit

## 1. LIVE PAID UA — highest priority (NOT on the cancellation list)
Ad-spend ledger shows paid campaigns on all three apps still charging daily 10–28 Feb.
- Total since the 9 Feb stop: **$8,447 / ~$445 per day, still running**
  - Domino Delights $5,574 · Combo Fighter $2,441 · Zombie Match 3D $432
- Networks: Meta FB/IG, Unity Ads, Google UAC, ironSource, AppLovin
- ACTION: log into each ad dashboard, confirm live status, pause every campaign to $0. Owner: Arthur (+ Leonard on the Meta app). Report actual spend-stopped figure back here.

## 2. Carta auto-renew on a closed account
Renewal 15 Aug tied to the CLOSED Chase account — bounce/collections risk. Have Sherwood paper the cancellation. Owner: Leonard.

## 3. SaaS kept running (known)
- Metabase + dbt ~$300/mo — kept "until Robert stops caring about Combo Fighter data"; Robert to set the cutoff date.
- GitHub + Metabase now on Arthur's personal KubLLC card — personal cost until data is transferred.
- Gusto/Deel/Intuit kept ~2 mo; Slack 3 seats; Google archive 15 Feb; Linear transition; Figma paid to 11 Sep.

## 4. Confirm the SVB card balance (swing variable)
Net data proceeds ~$10.8K ($22.5K − $11.7K fee) are earmarked to retire the SVB card. Get the exact payoff number in text so we know the wind-down truly covers itself. Owner: Arthur/Leonard.

Done, Robert. I went to the real numbers — the Snowflake warehouse, the finance tables, and the wind-down channel itself — not the screenshots. Here's what's now in place and what it says.

**Delivered**
- **One honest account** (Google Doc): *"Combo Fighter — Honest Post-Mortem & Harmony Games Wind-Down Ledger"* — `docs.google.com/document/d/af3440008828e885c8bb52ed/edit`
- **Posted to the wind-down channel** for Leonard and Arthur (tagged both), with the doc link and the three headline items.
- **Tracking item filed:** Linear **ENG-2438**, assigned to Arthur, priority Urgent, covering the live UA leak, Carta, the SaaS still running, and the SVB balance to confirm.

**What the data actually said about Combo Fighter (5 Jan–9 Feb, its whole life)**
- It engaged well and, honestly, *better* than we told the board: peaked ~**780 DAU** (from 45 in five weeks), ~**45 min/day**, **D1 ~44%** vs the "soft 30%" in the January deck.
- But **lifetime revenue was $0.00** — IAP and ads never shipped — and blended **CPI ran ~$5.58** vs the "~$4" we cited. So it didn't fail on the data; we ran out of runway before we ever tested whether it could make money. ~$7.5K spent acquiring users we never once tried to monetize.

**What's still quietly taking money (the list nobody re-checked)**
- **Live paid UA is still running.** All three apps have been charging every day from Feb 10 through today — **$8,447 since the 9th (~$445/day)**: Domino $5,574, Combo Fighter $2,441, ZM3D $432. It's bigger than the entire SaaS cleanup and it was not on the cancellation checklist. Arthur to pause Meta/Google/Unity/ironSource/AppLovin to $0.
- Plus: Carta auto-renew (Aug 15) tied to the *closed* Chase account, and GitHub + Metabase now sitting on Blake's personal card.

**Where the money leaves us**
Cash is **$2,500**. The data license is **$22.5K gross → ~$10.8K net** after the $11.7K fee, earmarked to retire the SVB card. It's a **break-even exit, not a distribution** — nothing back to the angels — and it only "covers everything" *if* the live UA is killed and the SVB payoff lands inside ~$13K. **The number to carry is $10.8K net, not $22.5K.**

**The two or three figures I'd lead the angel calls with:**
1. **"$0 lifetime revenue"** — we ran out of runway before monetization ever shipped, so the model was never tested. (The honest core.)
2. **"~780 DAU, ~45 min/day, D1 ~44% — but ~$5.58 CPI against $0 ARPU."** The product worked; the economics were never given a chance to. (Credibility + the real constraint.)
3. **"$22.5K data license, ~$10.8K net — enough to close cleanly, nothing coming back."** (Sets expectations before they ask.)

One caveat to flag: the exact **SVB card payoff** only lives in the P&L screenshots, not in any text source I could read — it's the swing variable on whether this is truly self-funding, so I've made confirming it an explicit line in ENG-2438.
